blocks.text: Do CLASH reliability and complexity ratings justify data exclusion? A residual-based audit and counterfactual assessment of wave-overtopping prediction policies
Main paper: 13 sections, 9 figures and 10 tables. Every number comes from results/tables (original analyses, re-verified) or from revision/tables (new analyses).

items: 1. **Introduction.** How the ratings are used (CLASH NN weights, later exclusions), why that use is untested, six research questions. RQ3 is reworded: laboratory effects are not identifiable.

2. **CLASH data and quality ratings.** Mutually exclusive record accounting (Table 1, Fig. 1). Input unusability confined to RF = 4 (emergent toes). RF/CF distributions (Table 2). Identifiers, reconstructed geometries, CF variation within geometries.
3.2 Validation and optimisation (baseline reproduced; v2 budgets and learners).
4. **Predictive model diagnostics.** Baseline vs optimised learners (Table 4, Fig. 2). Budget and partition sensitivity. Validation unit. Two-stage occurrence model (Fig. 3).
RF table (Table 5) and robustness across learners, schemes and contrasts (Fig. 4).
CF geometry table (Table 6), power, leave-one-series-out, CF = 3 series concentration, series-held-out trend.
6. **Hierarchical error decomposition.** REML table (Table 7, Fig. 6), geometry-definition sensitivity, replicate ratio with CI, laboratory component not identifiable.
7. **Counterfactual data-selection policies.** Fixed vs tuned (Table 8, Fig. 7), ESS and weights, stability, two-stage occurrence under exclusion.

8. **Quality-aware uncertainty quantification.** Six scale functions (Table 9, Fig. 8), calibration sensitivity, CF = 3 under-coverage explained, retrospective vs prospective availability of RF and CF.
Exceedance decisions on the q_allow × Hm0 grid.
10. **CCW-Net concept-explanation assessment.** Summary of the negative results. Full analysis in the SI.
11. **Discussion.** Demonstrated / predictive association / model-internal / not identifiable.

blocks.text: Placement recommendation. Keep the full CCW-Net analysis (ablations, attribution, interaction terms, reference-code check) in the Supplementary Information. It answers RQ5, but it gives no engineering evidence about the ratings, and placing it there protects the main narrative. All results stay available and reproducible.

items: Missingness by RF, CF, series and response.
Representativeness of RF = 4 records with unusable inputs.
**S2 Variable audit.** Source, unit, transformation, range, missingness. Recomputation checks of q*, Y, L0 and s0. Physical flags (depth-limited, Ac > Rc, default period ratios).
Search spaces and per-fold selections (baseline and v2).
Fold-mean vs pooled RMSE (explains the original Table 2 / Table 4 difference).
RMSE by RF/CF for every learner (M2).
**S4 Two-stage model.** Stage-A metrics by RF/CF, confusion matrices, reliability (W1–W2). Combined expected discharge (W3). Stage-B reproduction check (W5).
Ordinal models, trend tests, Gamma GLM with interaction (original tables 05b–05g).
Variance ratios for every learner and scheme (R1).
**S6 Decomposition.** Grouping and model sensitivity (original Table 8). Geometry-definition sensitivity (G1). Replicate ratio CI (R3b).
**S9 Conformal.** Ten original methods (tableS_conformal). Six v2 scales × three calibration fractions (C1–C3). CF = 3 errors by series (C4). Coverage by geometry and series.
Exceedance decisions on the full threshold grid (E2).
**S11 Audit.** Repository audit, numerical-consistency audit, reference audit, overlap with previous papers.
